source.title: Rényi Sharpness: A Novel Sharpness that Strongly Correlates with Generalization
source.authors: Qiaozhe Zhang; Jun Sun; Ruijie Zhang; Yingzhuang Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables and figures are flattened, but the main correlation claims and conditions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It measures associations between Hessian-based sharpness measures and the train-test loss gap using Kendall rank correlations, a conceptual test of whether measured network properties track generalization. Its Rényi measure is not the magnitude-aware sharpness named in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper's own Rényi-sharpness correlations and comparisons with other measures are relevant findings. Results from cited prior work are not recorded. Individual layer correlations appear in figures; the selected rows capture the paper's explicit task-level summaries rather than transcribing every plotted layer.
record.test_reason: The Rényi-sharpness rows do not test V7, but the study's own ASAM comparisons do bear on its magnitude-aware sharpness–gap relationship: ASAM measures loss increases under weight-scaled perturbations. This is an alternative operationalization, using a first-order loss surrogate rather than Jiang's training-error perturbation threshold. Training includes augmentation and does not enforce similarly low training loss, so these comparisons test an extension of V7's setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report strong Rényi-sharpness correlations and improved test accuracy with RSAM over the tested baselines. Their conclusion states a broader superiority over existing SAM methods, but their experiments establish comparisons only with the included methods and tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures normalized Hessian-spectrum Rényi sharpness and its correlation with the train-test loss gap. It does not test the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7. It also proposes RSAM, an approximate Rényi-sharpness regularizer.
record.method_sensitivity: Rényi order α; Hessian spectral profile; model and dataset; training hyperparameters varied to produce different minima; data augmentation is allowed during training but sharpness is computed without augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Rényi sharpness correlates with loss gaps across the six recorded training tasks, with alpha selected to maximize correlation; augmentation is used during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected-order normalized Hessian spectral entropy can rank generalization gaps within the tested vision architectures and training sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: Global Rényi sharpness has tau 0.8195 in the 56-model ImageNet ViT pool; last-layer Rényi sharpness has tau 0.6737 in the 72-model CLIP fine-tuning pool.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rényi sharpness can track loss gaps within the tested ImageNet transformer model pools.

record.code_released: The source code is publicly available at this link. (URL not included in supplied text.)
record.problems: The correlation experiments vary training hyperparameters and compare metrics, but correlation does not establish causality. The main paper's task summaries often rely on figures; individual layer coefficients are displayed in plots, and the supplied text does not give an aggregate coefficient for each task. Sharpness is computed on training subsets, without augmentation. Authors state the theoretical bounds rely on homogeneous or approximately homogeneous activations, and RSAM uses an approximate sharpness surrogate.
record.rows_left_out: The per-layer Rényi-sharpness coefficients and per-measure comparison coefficients in Figures 2–3 and Appendix K.2, K.3, and K.4 are not separately transcribed; the task-level summaries are retained. Table 9's log-det Hessian correlations are not extracted because log-det is not one of the claim versions' named measures. RSAM test-accuracy comparisons in Tables 1–2 are not extracted because they report the proposed training method's performance, not a test of a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled optimizer comparisons of held-out performance under limited versus broader tuning; varying optimizers to generate minima does not establish these comparisons.
Controlled batch-size effects on held-out performance and recovery through recipe changes; varying batches for correlation experiments does not establish these effects.
Controlled dropout addition or removal and its effects on test error.

The exact Jiang magnitude-aware training-error threshold measure; comparisons restricted to similarly low training loss without augmentation; SVHN; ranking against the original suite of margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized versus random training examples and retraining.

missing.what: Add V7-linked rows for the study's ASAM L2 and L-infinity correlations in convolutional models, including signed coefficients, training augmentation, the rho search, first-order approximation, and lack of a matched-low-loss selection criterion. Although comparison coefficients are declared omitted in rows_left_out, these are the measurements underlying the V7 verdicts and need dedicated rows.
missing.locator: Figure 2; Appendix K.2 Figures 9, 11–13; Appendices I.3–I.4, J.3.1 and J.5

record.verdict_notes: The extraction overlooked magnitude-aware ASAM baseline results when declaring every version untested. Rényi entropy and RSAM performance alone warrant no verdict on V7. Neither ASAM training-method accuracy nor cited prior findings are used as evidence here. The V7 verdicts rest on the study's own correlation measurements and remain limited to its alternative measure and training conditions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
The specified magnitude-aware perturbation measure, its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures, and comparisons at similarly low training loss.
Removing memorized examples and measuring retraining accuracy.

relationships.condition: ASAM loss-based magnitude-aware sharpness in augmented CIFAR-10 ResNet18/34 and TinyImageNet ResNet18 training sweeps.
relationships.reason: Text/figures, outside R1–R8: ASAM L2 Kendall tau is 0.0161, 0.0023 and 0.0698 respectively; L-infinity gives only 0.1954, 0.3103 and 0.2571. This weak tracking qualifies extension to these recipes and this surrogate; it does not refute the original controlled setting.
relationships.display_finding: The available evidence does not confirm the reported weak associations between ASAM sharpness and generalization gaps on CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet.

source_check.condition: ASAM loss-based magnitude-aware sharpness in augmented CIFAR-10 ResNet18/34 and TinyImageNet ResNet18 training sweeps.
source_check.reason: Figures 8, 9 and 13 report the stated near-zero L2 and weak positive L∞ correlations. These qualify extension to augmented training and this surrogate, without challenging V7's original controlled setting.

relationships.condition: ASAM loss-based magnitude-aware sharpness in augmented CIFAR-100 ResNet18/34 training sweeps.
relationships.reason: Text/figures, outside R1–R8: ASAM L2 Kendall tau is -0.4023 and -0.2460, while L-infinity gives -0.1126 and -0.0253. The expected positive association fails in these extended settings, with training-loss comparability unestablished.
relationships.display_finding: The available evidence does not confirm the reported negative associations between ASAM sharpness and generalization gaps on CIFAR-100.
